wa.tpl.formal_email.title: Formal Business Email
wa.tpl.formal_email.rule1: Always open with a formal salutation such as Dear Mr. / Ms. followed by the family name.
wa.tpl.formal_email.rule2: Pick the connector that expresses the right relationship; "and" and "but" also work when needed.
wa.tpl.formal_email.rule3: Use the future perfect to stress deadline commitment: "will have deployed".
wa.tpl.job_application.title: Job Application Cover Letter
wa.tpl.job_application.rule1: Name the position clearly in the first line.
wa.tpl.job_application.rule2: Tie your past achievements to the company's future goals.
wa.tpl.job_application.rule3: Close with a professional sign-off such as Sincerely or Respectfully.
wa.tpl.essay.title: Academic Opinion Essay
wa.tpl.essay.rule1: Open with a strong hook and topic sentence.
wa.tpl.essay.rule2: Support your opinion with real statistics and evidence.
wa.tpl.essay.rule3: Avoid slang like "cool, stuff, a lot of".
wa.tpl.complaint.title: Formal Complaint Letter
wa.tpl.complaint.rule1: Keep a calm formal tone without anger or excess emotion.
wa.tpl.complaint.rule2: Pin down the problem with numbers and dates: order number, delivery date.
wa.tpl.complaint.rule3: Use the future perfect for your time expectations: "will have investigated".
wa.tpl.university.title: University Application Essay
wa.tpl.university.rule1: Open with a short personal story linking your passion to the field.
wa.tpl.university.rule2: Cite concrete achievements with numbers: projects, volunteer hours.
wa.tpl.university.rule3: Link your past to your future with the future perfect: "will have completed".

wa.mistakes.title: Most Common Writing Mistakes
wa.mistakes.sub: Avoid these three slips that drag down your score in academic and professional writing:
wa.mistake1.title: Joining independent clauses without proper punctuation (Run-on Sentences)
wa.mistake1.explanation: Do not join two complete sentences without a time connector or proper comma.
wa.mistake2.title: The subject-verb agreement trap
wa.mistake2.explanation: "Every" is always singular, so it takes "has", not "have".
wa.mistake3.title: The trap of using "will" after time connectors
wa.mistake3.explanation: After "By the time" we use the present simple (arrive) for future meaning.

ab.title: About Henglish Academy
ab.intro: Henglish brings together vocabulary, grammar, listening, speaking, reading, writing and pronunciation. Learn and understand, then use English in movies, games, situations and the 3D world. Track your progress with tests.
ab.lessonsIntro: Examples, images and dialogues connect vocabulary and grammar to everyday use.
ab.feedbackIntro: Tips in Egyptian Arabic and feedback on common learning pitfalls.
ab.achievementsIntro: Completion certificates, achievement badges and progress saved in your browser.
ab.learnIntro: Plain Egyptian Arabic explanations make ideas easier to understand.
ab.useIntro: Put learning into practice with interactive exercises, sentence-building games and question banks.
ab.ownIntro: Practise pronunciation and conversations for work, airports and interviews.
ab.why: Why we built this learning experience
ab.whyIntro: Memorizing rules is not enough. Learning words without context does not make speaking easier. We combine understanding and practice: listen and read, speak and write, then review through varied situations and challenges.
ab.design: The platform brings together a dark visual design, audio pronunciation, interactive games and a personal progress dashboard to support regular practice.
ab.mission: Built for Arabic-speaking and international learners.

sp.transfer.title: Make the conversation your own
sp.transfer.intro: Optional follow-up: use this lesson topic in a new situation. Plan briefly, then record an original reply. No model answer or automatic grade.
sp.transfer.note: Notes stay only in this open practice and are not sent, saved or graded. Switching tasks, closing or leaving the lesson discards notes and recordings.
sp.transfer.record.0: Give your own English reply with a changed detail.
sp.transfer.record.1: Continue the conversation in your own English words.
sp.transfer.task.A1.0: Keep the lesson topic. Change one name, place or time and say two short sentences about yourself. You may invent details.
sp.transfer.task.A1.1: Ask one simple follow-up question about this topic. Then give a short possible answer.
sp.transfer.task.A2.0: Change where or when this situation happens. Explain your new plan in three sentences. You may invent details.
sp.transfer.task.A2.1: Add a small problem to this situation. Ask for help politely and suggest one solution.
sp.transfer.task.B1.0: Choose a different goal for this situation. Explain what you want, give a reason and ask the other person a question.
sp.transfer.task.B1.1: Imagine the other person disagrees. Acknowledge their point and suggest a practical compromise.
sp.transfer.task.B2.0: Change an important assumption in this situation. Compare two responses and explain which you would choose and why.
sp.transfer.task.B2.1: Continue with a respectful counterargument, a supporting example and a question that invites the other person to respond.
